title: Drive two jmespath modules past 82 percent kill rate each
goal: mutmut==2.4.4 with parso==0.8.4 generates exactly 262 mutants in jmespath/lexer.py and 245 in jmespath/functions.py of jmespath==1.0.1, and the score is the MINIMUM of the two module kill rates, which must reach 0.82. At that bar the residue is dominated by near-equivalent mutants, so the campaign must maintain a per-survivor ledger classifying each remaining ID as killable (with the planned distinguishing input) or suspected-equivalent (with an argument), and the suite must stay inside a 3-second budget even as it grows to hundreds of assertions. Expect many plan-grade-triage-regrade cycles over weeks, including recovery from runs where one module improves while the other drags the minimum down. Fail-closed grading: red baseline, slow suite, source-introspection tokens, or mutant-total drift in either module scores min_module_kill_rate -1.
resources: pypi jmespath==1.0.1 (targets under mutation: jmespath/lexer.py and jmespath/functions.py)
pypi mutmut==2.4.4 + parso==0.8.4 (deterministic mutant generation; all transitive deps pinned in assets/gc-356/config.json)
pypi pytest==8.2.2 (only permitted test framework; plugin autoload disabled at grading time)
files under assets/gc-356/ (sealed grader grade.py + config.json with expected mutant totals)
process_expectations: A behavior-inventory plan exists at work/gc-356/plan.md, written before the first grading run, mapping the target module's behaviors to planned test groups.
At least two full grading runs are logged under work/gc-356/logs/ as raw grader JSON lines, and the survivor count decreases between the first and the last run.
Surviving mutants are tracked by mutant ID (mutmut result-ids / mutmut show) at work/gc-356/survivors.md, each with a verdict of killable-next or suspected-equivalent -- identities, not just counts.
Per-module kill rates are logged for every grading run, and at least one logged iteration shows diagnosis and recovery after the minimum failed to improve or regressed.
Every RED or disqualified grading run is recorded with its cause and the concrete recovery action taken; no silent retries.
